  - text: CLASS 8 · PRACTICAL GEOMETRY
  - heading "Right Triangle Construction by RHS" [level=1]
  - paragraph: "Learning objective: Construct a right triangle from the hypotenuse and one corresponding side."
  - text: "♧ Class: 8 ▣ Topic: Practical Geometry ◷ Duration: 20 min ♧ Method: RHS (Right angle–Hypotenuse–Side)"

  - paragraph: "Use Thales’ theorem: A point on the semicircle with diameter AB makes ∠ACB = 90°."
  - button "Reset":

    - slider "Set length AC 5 cm": "5"
    - complementary: Move point C on the semicircle so that AC equals the chosen length.
    - heading "3 Construct point C" [level=3]
    - paragraph: With center A and radius AC, draw an arc to cut the semicircle at C.
    - paragraph: Triangle ABC is the required right triangle.

    - img "RHS triangle on Thales semicircle":

      - text: 8 cm 5 cm A B C
    - heading "Length check" [level=3]
    - paragraph: ✓ AB (hypotenuse) = 8.00 cm
    - paragraph: ✓ AC (chosen leg) = 5.00 cm
    - paragraph: ✓ BC (other leg) = 6.24 cm
    - heading "Thales’ theorem" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Since C lies on the semicircle with diameter AB,
    - text: ∠ACB = 90°.
    - img
  - article:
    - heading "▣ Why it works" [level=2]
    - paragraph: By Thales’ theorem, any point on the semicircle with diameter AB subtends a right angle at C.
    - paragraph: Hence, ∠ACB = 90° and △ABC is a right triangle. Setting AC fixes one leg, and AB is the hypotenuse.
    - img
    - text: C on semicircle with diameter AB ⇒ ∠ACB = 90°
  - article:
    - heading "▣ Worked example" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Construct a right triangle with hypotenuse 8 cm and one leg 5 cm.
    - list:
      - listitem: Draw AB = 8 cm.
      - listitem: Draw the semicircle with diameter AB.
      - listitem: With center A, radius 5 cm, cut it at C.
      - listitem: Join AC and CB. Then ∠ACB = 90°.
    - img
    - strong: "Result: AB = 8 cm, AC = 5 cm, BC = 6.24 cm."
  - article:
    - heading "⚠ Common mistake" [level=2]
    - text: Treating a leg as the hypotenuse.
    - paragraph: Using a side other than the longest side as the diameter breaks Thales’ theorem and gives the wrong triangle.
    - img: ×

    - heading "⚑ Mini challenge" [level=2]

    - paragraph: "Goal: Place C on the semicircle so that AC = 6 cm."
